title: Earthly Extravaganza
changes: New: Earthlike worlds are finished. Choose "Earthlike" when you make a world for a world 640 blocks tall and 1024 or 2048 wide, with mountains, seas and rivers, 21 biomes, rocks and soils that fit their place, trees by climate, ground plants, wild crops and animals. They're no longer a preview: the "Playable early" note is gone, and their land won't change in later updates.

New: you can make the Earthlike blocks: the four new woods' planks, sticks, Crafting Bench, Cutter, doors and fences, as with the other woods; the 21 rocks back from their cobbled blocks in the Kiln; Bricks and Polished blocks (Polished Andesite too) at the Crafting Bench with a pickaxe; and Pink, Blue and White Dye from Fireweed, Gentian and Edelweiss.

New: survival in an Earthlike world: dig Earthlike gravel by hand for Rocks, the start of a Crude Axe; get Clay Balls from Clay Soil, Cracked Clay and Silt; and make Fireclay with any Earthlike gravel.
New: Burnt Logs burn as fuel in a Kiln or Foundry, and split into Sticks with an axe.
New: river water moves. Ripples slide downstream at the river's own pace, the rapids foam, and waterfalls stream down.
New: the main menu shows an Earthlike rainforest river.
Fixed: in the web version, digging Earthlike soils and ground by hand gave the wrong pieces; now you get the block itself. Mud and Peat dug by hand now give pieces, as they do in the desktop version.

New: Earthlike worlds come to life. Trees grow by climate, including four new woods: tall Mahogany in rainforests, flat-topped Acacia on the savanna, Stiltroot standing in shallow swamp water, and Teak in dry forests. Old burns hold burnt trees on Charred Ground.
New: 21 kinds of ground plants grow across Earthlike land by biome: prairie grasses, forest ferns and Tree Ferns, flower clearings, marsh reeds, bog cotton grass, seaweed and more.

New: wild crops grow in Earthlike worlds where they belong: Potatoes in meadows and alpine lands, Flax in meadows and on the plains, Turnips in snowy lands and the taiga, Corn on the plains and savanna, Cantaloupes near deserts and badlands, and Dead Bushes in the dry lands.
New: Mahogany, Acacia, Stiltroot and Teak saplings grow into their trees.

New: animals live in Earthlike worlds, each in the lands that suit it. Cows graze the grassy soils, which grow back; goats climb the rocky ground; boar root under the trees. Rivers carry animals along, as they carry you.
New: in Earthlike worlds, mobs spawn at night on the grassy soils too.
Changed: Earthlike worlds you've already made grow the new trees, plants and animals too, apart from the spots you've changed, so one could even sprout inside a building.

New: Earthlike rivers now run downhill: gently over flat land, quickly down slopes and in rapids down steep ones, and where a river drops 2 blocks or more its water falls. A river carries you along, and anything you drop floats off downstream. Wading in the shallows pushes you half as hard, and you can't swim up falling water.
New: you can hear rivers nearby, a soft rush beside calm water and a louder roar by rapids.
New: a block taken out of a river fills back in with running water.
Changed: Earthlike worlds you've already made get running rivers too, apart from the spots you've changed.

New: Earthlike worlds (preview). When you make a world, choose "Earthlike (preview)" for a world 640 blocks tall and 1024 or 2048 wide with realistic land: mountains, seas, lakes and rivers, rocks and soils that fit their place, and trees that grow by climate. It's playable early, so your Earthlike worlds may change or break in later updates. Older versions don't show Earthlike worlds.

New: the blocks made so far for the coming Earthly Extravaganza update are in the creative inventory: soils, ground blocks like Tundra Moss and Salt Crust, new plants, ores in rock like Copper Ore in Granite, and 4 new woods (Mahogany, Acacia, Stiltroot and Teak) with their doors, fences and shapes. They have no recipes yet, and the 4 new saplings can't grow yet.
New: the new grassy soils count as Grass, and the bare soils as Dirt, for planting saplings, flowers and crops and for tilling with a hoe.
A tilled soil becomes Tilled Dirt, so if you leave it dry with nothing planted it turns back into Dirt, not the soil it was.

New: 21 kinds of rock. Dig into a new world and you'll find patches of 11 of them in the Andesite: Limestone, Shale, Chalk, Slate, Marble, Quartzite, Schist, Gneiss, Basalt, Granite and Gabbro. All 21 are in the creative inventory, with their cobbled blocks, bricks and polished blocks where they have them, their shapes and their gravels.
Stone is now called Andesite: Cobblestone is now Cobbled Andesite, Stone Bricks are Andesite Bricks and Chiseled Stone is Chiseled Andesite. They work just the same.
Most blocks, animals and mobs have been redrawn with up to 7 shades, for a bit more depth.
Larch, Holly, Birch, Aspen, Cedar, Willow, Orange, Cypress and Palm wood have new colours, so every wood is easier to tell apart.
Fixed: in the web version, a survival world's inventory is kept when you leave and come back.
Behind the scenes: worlds are now stored in a new way, ready for much bigger worlds. Your worlds look and play the same, and stay playable in older versions.

title: Fields and Flocks
changes: New: Potatoes, Turnips, Flax, Corn and Cantaloupes to grow on tilled soil. Plant a Potato, a Turnip or Corn itself, and Flax and Cantaloupe from their seeds. Corn grows two blocks tall, a grown Cantaloupe vine grows melons beside it one at a time, and Turnips grow just as fast on dry soil
New: crops growing wild in new Biomes worlds: Potatoes and Flax in meadows, Turnips in snowy lands and the taiga, Corn on the plains, and Cantaloupes near deserts and badlands
New: Dead Bushes in the deserts and badlands of new Biomes worlds. Break one by hand for a Stick or two, or dig it up whole with a shovel
New: Baked Potatoes, Roasted Corn and Cooked Eggs from the Kiln, plus Turnips, Cantaloupe Slices and Truffles to eat
New: Clay Jugs, fired in the Kiln from 3 Clay Balls. Use one on a Goat you've fed for a Jug of Milk, and drinking it gives the jug back
New: Flax gives Linen and String. Linen makes Linen Cloth in 13 colours, which can be cut at the Cutter into slabs, stairs, quarters and pieces

New: the Linen Bag (Crafting Bench: 3 Linen, 1 String) holds a mix of things in one slot, up to a stack in all. Drop things onto it in your inventory, and right-click it to take the last one back out. It looks fuller once it holds anything, and a blue bar shows how full it is

New: a fence for every wood (4 from 4 planks and 2 Sticks at the Crafting Bench). Fences join up with each other, walls and doors, so a door in a fence line makes a gate, and they're too tall for you or animals to jump
New: six animals in Biomes worlds, old and new: Chickens, Ducks, Deer, Goats, Boar and Bears. Feed one its food to make it happy, and happy animals have young
New: fed Chickens and Ducks lay Eggs. Chickens scratch tilled soil, sometimes fertilizing it, but peck at young crops. A Duck swimming by a field makes its crops grow a little faster
New: Deer run from you unless you hold fruit or Grain. They plant saplings as they roam, and nibble young ones
New: Goats eat Dead Bushes and wild shrubs, and give milk into a Clay Jug once fed
New: Boar root up grass near Oaks and Maples, sometimes turning up a Truffle, and fight back when hit
New: Bears hunt Chickens, Ducks, Deer and Boar, and leave you alone unless you hit one or go near its cubs
New: Ice can be cut into slabs, stairs, quarters and pieces at the Cutter
Changed: Cows have a sturdier new look, with a tufted tail, and lower their heads all the way to the grass when they graze
Changed: doors swing open on their hinges like real doors, sticking out of the doorway (even into a block beside it)
Changed: Fireclay Casing has Fireclay Bricks on top and Fireclay Terracotta underneath
Changed: Fireclay Terracotta has the new terracotta look
Changed: corner shadows are a little lighter, so narrow holes, tight corners and tunnels aren't so dark
Fixed: pieces, slabs, stairs and quarters looked too bright beside whole blocks. They're now shaded the same way, and grass and leaf ones take the biome's colour
Fixed: after loading a world on the desktop version, the space under a roof built higher than the land around it could be lit as brightly as open sky
Fixed: a grazing calf's head no longer comes away from its shoulders
Fixed: a friend picking up a dropped tool in your world now gets it as worn as it was

title: Trees and Leaves
changes: New: 12 new trees in new Biomes worlds: Cedar and Maple in the woods; Birch, Aspen and Holly among the taiga's firs, with rare groves of giant Redwoods; Cherry trees in meadows; Cypress in swamps; Juniper and bare Dead trees in the badlands (Dead trees in deserts too); Larch and Holly in the snowy lands; Orange groves and Palo Verde at the desert's edges
New: the plains are now prairie, with lone wide-crowned prairie oaks and low oak shrubs

New: 12 new woods (Cedar, Maple, Birch, Aspen, Redwood, Cherry, Cypress, Juniper, Larch, Holly, Orange, Palo Verde), each with logs, stripped logs, planks, leaves and all their slabs, stairs and pieces. Also Dead Logs (6 Sticks by hand)
New: Cherries, Oranges and Juniper Berries to eat, from their trees' leaves (1 in 4 when broken without a Hoe)

New: doors for all 16 woods. 6 planks make 2 at the Crafting Bench. Right-click opens and shuts a door, and it swings away from you. Its hinge goes on the side you click. Two doors side by side open together. Cows can't open them

New: saplings for all 16 trees, in the creative Natural tab. Leaves now and then drop their sapling (1 in 10 when broken without a Hoe). Plant one on Grass, Dirt, Snowy Grass, Swamp Grass, Mud or Peat (Palm, Orange and Palo Verde on Sand too)
New: a sapling grows into its tree after about 10 minutes, once it has room. A growing tree never breaks anything you've built
New: an Oak sapling in the plains grows a prairie oak. Four Redwood saplings in a square grow one giant Redwood
New: Bone Ash on a sapling has a 1 in 3 chance of growing it at once
Changed: Dates have a black outline, like every other item
Fixed: in Survival, right-click puts down the block in your hand even when your offhand holds something (the offhand is used when your hand holds nothing you can put down)
Fixed: on desktop, the mouse pointer is let go as soon as the game window loses focus (Alt+Tab or clicking another window); click back in the game to look around again
Worlds made before this update stay exactly as they were; the new trees grow in new Biomes worlds

title: The Order of Things
changes: New: Fireclay can be made at the Crafting Bench from Clay, Sand and Gravel
New: in Survival, the tools in your tool slots show in a row above the hotbar, with their wear bars, and the one last picked for you is highlighted
Fixed: cows' hearts (and the puff from a Snowball) glowed in the dark and showed through fog
Changed: ores match the new Stone look
Fixed: Sandstone dropped nothing when broken in Survival
Fixed: on the web, the world's music came back in the main menu after you quit, and mobs and sounds carried on for a moment while quitting
Changed: each block's slab, stair, quarter and piece pictures now come from one picture sheet per block (behind the scenes; blocks look the same)
Fixed: sand stairs showed a stray sliver of sand's middle patch

New: the creative inventory has 9 tabs (Building, Natural, Wood, Shapes, Light & Decoration, Tools & Armor, Food, Materials, Machines), and a search box that looks through all of them, shapes too. Shapes lists every piece, slab, stairs and quarter, so the + button is gone
New: Snowy Grass, Swamp Grass, Ice, Chocolate and the Smoldering, Burnt and Ever Torches are now in the creative inventory
New: in creative, a Clear hotbar button. Dragging a hotbar slot onto the tabs or the list empties it
New: middle-click picks the block you're looking at: in creative it goes in your hand; in survival it selects it if it's in your hotbar
New: survival inventory: click a slot to pick up its stack and carry it on the mouse, then click to put it down, add it to the same item, or swap. Right-click picks up half a stack, or puts down one
New: drag a carried stack across slots to share it out evenly (right-drag puts one in each). Double-click gathers the same item into one stack
New: shift-click moves a stack across your slots (hotbar, pockets, backpack). Tools, armor, backpacks and belts go straight into their own slots first
New: a Sort button tidies your pockets and backpack: the same items merged into full stacks, in the creative tabs' order

New: Q drops one item (the selected hotbar slot, or the slot under the mouse in a screen); Ctrl+Q or Shift+Q drops the whole stack. Clicking outside a screen drops the stack you're carrying; closing the screen puts it back

New: the recipe book (in your inventory and at the Crafting Bench) has a search and a Can make now switch, and shows each recipe's ingredients as pictures with how many you have: red when you're short, with what's missing
New: How to make: press R over any item, or click an ingredient's picture, to see every way to make it (by hand, Crafting Bench, Cutter, Kiln or Foundry), or that it's only found in the world
New: the Cutter has a search and a Can make now switch, and shows how many blocks a cut needs and how many you have
New: tooltips on every slot: the name, how worn a tool or piece of armor is, how many hearts a food heals, and how long a fuel burns

New: in survival, an armor bar mirrors your hearts on the other side of the hotbar, filling in quarters with how much protection your armor gives right now, so worn armor shows less. It only shows while you're wearing armor
Changed: a clearer pause screen: Back to game, then Settings, Skin and Multiplayer side by side, then Save world, with the ways to quit set apart below
Changed: settings are in four tabs: Video, Sound, Controls (with every key listed) and Game

Changed: in survival, the offhand slot sits closer to the hotbar, and your tool row sits centred on the line above the hotbar, between your hearts and your armor bar. A tool row too long to fit between them gets its own line just above the hotbar, with your hearts and armor bar above it. Notes always show above everything
Changed: on the web, menus with lots of item pictures open faster
Changed: on the web, middle-click no longer starts the browser's auto-scroll, and Shift+Q works everywhere
Fixed: on desktop, the pause screen's Save & quit to main menu button was missing
Fixed: on desktop, Sandstone was missing from the creative inventory
Fixed: on the web, a Rock, Clay Ball or Brick lying on snow was harder to aim at than it looked
Changed: Snowy Grass and Swamp Grass now sound like grass, Ice like glass, and the Cutter like wood (they all sounded like stone)

Changed: the game's blocks, recipes, mobs and other lists now come from shared data files that the web and desktop editions both read, so they can't drift apart (behind the scenes; nothing plays differently)

title: Shaped by Nature
changes: New: natural structures in new Biomes worlds: stone arches and rock spires in deserts and badlands, sea stacks off the coast, fallen giant trees (hollow, so you can walk through) in forests and swamps, sinkholes in plains and meadows, boulder fields in the cold lands, and swamp hollows
Changed: in new worlds, tree trunks go all the way up into their leaves
Worlds made before this update stay exactly as they were
New: logs lie the way you put them down: on a side they lie pointing out from it, on a top or bottom they stand up. Fallen giant trees now lie on their sides
New: GUI scale slider in Settings: Auto, or 1x to 4x (always a whole number, so pixels stay even)

New: Snow Block, and Snow that lies in layers: put Snow on Snow to add a layer (8 make a Snow Block); you sink into one layer, deeper snow is solid; it falls off (as Snowballs) if what it lies on goes; breaking it gives 2-4 Snowballs for each layer (a Snow Block gives 4), and 4 Snowballs make a Snow Block (which makes 8 Snow). Snowy lands in new worlds are covered in a layer of snow, trees and all
New: Fir, Palm and Willow Leaves each have their own new look, and still take on the biome's colour
Changed: taiga grass and leaves are a little cooler and bluer
Fixed: you only step up onto slabs, stairs, quarters and pieces, not onto whole blocks from a slab, the Cutter or snow

New: snowlogging: torches, flowers, Rocks, Clay Balls and Bricks lying on the ground, the Cutter, and slabs, stairs, quarters and pieces can share their space with one layer of Snow. Put Snow on them, or put them down in a layer of snow. It's only ever one layer, and breaking the block leaves the snow behind
New: in snowy lands, snow lies on the ground under the trees too
Changed: slabs, stairs, quarters, pieces, snow layers, torches and the Cutter (with its saw blade) show their real 3D shape in your hand and in your inventory; items and flowers stay flat pictures
Changed: slabs, stairs, quarters and pieces of many blocks have their own pictures on their cut sides, so they look neat instead of cut off

Changed: two slabs in one space stay a double slab (you can see the two halves), and pieces no longer join up into slabs, stairs or whole blocks: each piece stays its own little block. Breaking a double slab takes one slab at a time, and each piece breaks on its own
Changed: new looks for Stone and Cobblestone (and their deep layers), every colour of Terracotta, Grass and Swamp Grass

New: a layer of Snow can cover the tops of slabs, stairs (both steps), quarters and pieces, and the ground beside them, even ones with nothing under them. It's one layer, so you walk through it. Breaking the slab or stairs takes its snow too: it's left as a layer if the block below can hold snow, otherwise it drops as Snowballs
New: Snowball, a new item (also in the creative Items list): right-click to throw it, with its own throwing sound; it bursts into snow where it lands and knocks back mobs and players a little
Changed: the game's pictures are packed into a smaller texture, so it should work on more graphics cards and phones
New: Snow and the Snow Block have their own crunchy sounds for placing, breaking and walking on them (walking through anything snowed-in crunches too), and a Snowball lands with a soft splat
New: a Rock, Clay Ball or Brick put down on a layer of snow lies on top of it
Changed: a torch in snow keeps its snow when it burns down, smoulders or is lit again; a torch on a wall falls off when its wall goes, but the snow stays
Changed: a Clay Ball in snow still dries into a Brick, and keeps its snow
Changed: right-clicking a Cutter that stands in snow still opens it
Changed: a thrown Rock or Snowball flies as its flat picture instead of a little cube
New: anything thrown, Skeletons' Rocks included, makes a whoosh as it flies
New: choose how big a new world is, from 256 to 2048 blocks across
New: choose how big the biomes are in a new Biomes world, from half size to 4 times as big
Changed: the main menu no longer has a world open behind it. Pick a world from Singleplayer to play, and quitting to the main menu closes it (saving it first)
Worlds take much less memory: blocks are now stored chunk by chunk, so a new 1280 x 1280 world needs about 120 MB instead of 300 MB, and there's no longer a limit of 256 kinds of block
New worlds have biomes (choose "Biomes" when you make a world; older worlds stay as they were): Woods, Plains, Meadows, Taiga, Snowy lands, Deserts, Badlands and Swamps
Plains: flat, open grassland with flowers and a lone tree here and there
Meadows: gently rolling grass packed with flowers of every colour (the place to find dyes), with a few more trees than the plains
Taiga: thick Fir forests on ordinary grass, between the woods and the snowy lands, so the cold comes on gradually
Deserts: rolling sand dunes dotted with Palm trees, with Sandstone under the sand
Badlands: steep hills striped with coloured Terracotta (plain, orange, yellow, red, white and pink), next to the deserts: dig them for coloured terracotta without any dye
Snowy lands: Snowy Grass, pointed Fir trees, and seas and lakes frozen over with Ice
Swamps: low, flat, boggy land with shallow muddy pools, lots of clay, Willow trees with drooping leaves, and Mud and Peat under the grass
New blocks: Sandstone, Snowy Grass, Ice and Swamp Grass (digging up any grass gives Dirt; hoes till it and flowers plant on it)
New water picture: ripples, and a softer outline so seas and lakes no longer look like a grid
New looks for the terracottas, Sand, Sandstone, Clay, Fireclay, Leaves, the grass side, the Crafting Bench and the Cutter
Swamp Grass has its own picture (murky green with darker patches, and moss hanging over the side), and Snowy Grass has a snowy side

Grass and leaves take on the colour of the climate they grow in, fading smoothly from biome to biome: bluer near the snow, yellower near deserts, murkier in swamps, brighter in plains (Biome worlds only)

New wood: Fir, from the snowy lands' trees. Fir Log, Stripped Fir Log, Fir Planks (they make Sticks, Crafting Benches and Cutters, and cut into slabs and stairs like any planks) and Fir Leaves (the leaf picture, coloured a darker blue-green on top of the climate colour); logs and planks burn in the Kiln
The original wood is now called Oak: Oak Log, Stripped Oak Log, Oak Planks and Oak Leaves

New wood: Palm, from the desert's trees, and Willow, from the swamp's. Each has a Log, Stripped Log, Planks (Sticks, Crafting Benches and Cutters, slabs and stairs) and Leaves in their own colour; logs and planks burn in the Kiln
Dates: breaking Palm Leaves sometimes drops Dates, a food you can only find in the desert

Desert stone: Sandstone Bricks and Chiseled Sandstone (Sandstone at the Crafting Bench, with a pickaxe), and Smooth Sandstone (Sandstone fired in the Kiln). Sandstone and its blocks now need a pickaxe, and cut into slabs and stairs
Mud: the swamp's ground. Dig it with a shovel (by hand you get Mud Pieces); the Kiln fires it into Mud Bricks, a new building block
Peat: found under the swamp's mud. It's the best Kiln fuel: one Peat smelts 8 things (a log only smelts 4)
New worlds are four times bigger: 1280 x 1280 blocks instead of 640 x 640 (worlds you already have stay the size they are)
The main menu has a panorama: a view of this update's new biomes (badlands, palms, swamp and taiga) slowly turns behind the title
Fixed Zombies and Grr Angry hitting you through walls, floors and ceilings (from a cave under you, say)
The Foundry's Furnace has a Fireclay Bricks top and a new brown front
The Crafting Bench no longer lists the deep stone blocks, which aren't in the game yet

New block: the Cutter (3 Planks + a Copper Brick at the Crafting Bench), half a block tall with a spinning saw blade on top, cuts blocks into pieces, slabs and stairs; the Crafting Bench is just for crafting now

title: Pack & Plate
changes: Armor: helmets, chestplates, leggings and boots in leather, copper, iron, bronite, rosium and steel; they soak up hits and wear out
Backpacks (5 to 40 more slots) and Utility Belts (more offhand slots and 2 to 7 more tool slots), worn on your back and waist
A bigger survival inventory: 10 Pockets, tool slots that pick the right tool for you, and an offhand (R picks, F swaps, right-click uses it)
The inventory is laid out side by side: your slots on the left, crafting on the right, the same in the web and desktop editions
Ores: Copper, Iron, Tin and Gold, each needing a good enough pickaxe
Fireclay, its bricks and blocks, and the Foundry, which melts ore Chunks into Bricks and mixes alloys: Bronite, Rosium and Steel
Metal tools in copper, iron, bronite, rosium and steel
Tools wear out with use and break; a bar shows how much is left
Bedrock lines the bottom of the world
Sand, Gravel and Dirt fall when there's nothing under them
Plays multiplayer with web version Beta 0.1.0.0
Fixed see-through walls of water showing inside the sea near the edge of the world
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.9.5
Cows: they wander and graze on grass, and happy cows show pink hearts
Happy cows with room around them may have a calf, which follows the grown-ups and grows up after a while
Crowded cows don't mate, and once a chunk has 8 cows (calves and fat cows count) none of them breed
Feed a cow Grain to fatten it up: the more it has been fed, the more Raw Meat it drops
Cows with more room grow a bigger hide and drop more Leather
Cook Raw Meat into Cooked Meat in the kiln
Crops grow at random: some plants get ahead and some lag a little, so a field doesn't all ripen at once
Render distance slider in Settings (4 to 32 chunks): land past it isn't drawn and fades into the haze
Only the chunks within your render distance are built, so worlds load faster
Mobs only keep going within the render distance; cows further away wait where they are
Mobs now wait while you're paused, like the rest of the world
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.9.4
The world is drawn in 32x32x32 groups of chunks: far fewer pieces to draw each frame, so the game spends much less time on every frame
Chunks are still built as 16x16x16 cubes, so breaking and placing blocks stays fast
The world loads one 32x32x32 group at a time, nearest first
Chunks are now 16x16x16 cubes, stacked 12 high, instead of tall 16x16 columns
Digging, building, water and torches rebuild only the cubes around them, so changing a block is about 8 times faster
Empty sky isn't built at all, and caves and hilltops out of view are skipped on their own
Tools in your hand are 50% bigger, and the Hoe is turned the right way round
Your hand shows the whole arm now, running right off the edge of the screen
Fixed the arm jittering when you sprint-jump
Clay Balls dry into Bricks in 2 minutes instead of 5
New recipe: 4 Clay Balls pack back into a Clay block
Dirt and Gravel have swapped sounds
Leaves only drop themselves when mined with a Hoe; anything else just has the 1 in 5 chance of a Stick
The GUI is one size smaller, still in whole pixels
Farming! Right-click Grass or Dirt with a Hoe to till it into soil (tilling Grass sometimes turns up Grain Seeds)
Plant Grain Seeds on tilled soil; Grain grows through 8 stages, and ripe Grain gives Grain plus 1-2 seeds
Soil joined to water (through other tilled soil, up to 5 blocks away) is wet and grows Grain twice as fast
Bone Ash fertilizes soil for 2 harvests and makes Grain grow faster still
Dry tilled soil with nothing planted turns back into Dirt after a few minutes
Grain -> Flour by hand, Flour -> Bread in the Kiln; Bread is food
The Zombie is the night mob now, taking over from Grr Angry
New mob: the Skeleton comes out in the dark, keeps its distance and throws Rocks at you. It burns in daylight and drops Bones
New mob: the Gloomling lives deep underground in the pitch dark and snuffs out burning torches. It fades away if you come near holding a lit torch
Defeat a Gloomling to get a Gloom Wisp
Bones smelt into Bone Ash in the Kiln
White Dye is now made from Bone Ash, and Black Dye from a Gloom Wisp
The arrow keys look around too, as a backup for laptops
Fixed looking around with the mouse on PCs where the mouse wouldn't turn the camera
Slabs, stairs, quarters and pieces now show as little 3D models in the inventory, as sharp as full blocks
Dropped blocks, slabs, stairs, pieces and torches are now little 3D models instead of flat pictures
Tools are held properly: gripped near the end of the handle and turned side-on, so you swing with the head, not the flat
Tools in your hand are 1 pixel thick, for a little depth
Blocks in your inventory, hotbar and recipes show as little 3D cubes, including the kiln (with its opening); torches show as a small 3D stick
The + on blocks with other forms is smaller, neatly centred and tucked into the slot's bottom-right corner
Menus and the hotbar scale with your screen's display scaling by a whole number (150% makes them twice as big), so every pixel stays even

title: Shape & Shade
changes: Skin menu: paint your own player skin, with a turning 3D preview
Your hand now wears your skin
New player figure with elbows and knees
Other players look like players in their own skin, holding their items
New letters, numbers and symbols
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.7.0
Holding a torch now lights up the area around you, so you can see in dark caves and at night
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.6.1

title: Brick & Bloom
changes: Terracotta, Chiseled Terracotta and Bricks in 12 colours
Flowers grow in small patches on grass; pick them and plant them again
12 Dyes from flowers, Burnt Torches and Rocks, plus mixing for more colours
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.6.0
Cubeland as a desktop program for Windows, made in Godot, with the same version number as the web game
Plays multiplayer with the web version: host or join with the same 5-letter codes
Uses your font and menu pictures, like the web version
